summary:
A Victorian terrace of three. Two mirrored red-brick end houses with cream canted bays, stoops and small black-slate mansards with dormers stand either side of a taller cream-stucco centre house with a quartz portico, a balcony and a bracketed flat parapet. They share a plinth, a string course and a cornice line, and the roofline steps up in the middle, so the row reads as three separate houses that belong together. I checked the roof spec on a mock shell: the mansards built with no warnings. The centre house's flat roof gives one warning (the deck is a single material), which I left because the parapet hides the deck from the street. Victorian terrace: red-brick A and C with canted bays and slate mansards flank a taller cream-stucco B with quartz portico, balcony and bracketed parapet.
Two party-wall chimney stacks with lit campfires, four hearths, three stair wells, street, trees and walled rear gardens.
Six parts along the trades: shell, stairs, roofs, chimneys, fenestration and front, grounds.

masonry shell: Masonry shell built: plinth, brick A/C and sandstone B walls, party walls with pilasters, quoins, string course, canted bay bodies and floors y2/7/12/17. Openings, wells, stack cells and bay decks are left as air. make.sh clean, no refusals; check shows no floating blocks.
polish: Bay window frames show 8 orphan sandstone blocks until the front part glazes and the roofs part decks them
Rear corner quoins not built
plan.md and elements.md checklist items were not ticked (plan.md has no checkboxes; the elements.md sed failed on macOS)

summary:
stairs: Stairs part built in parts/stairs.mjs: seven four-riser spruce flights (A and C floors 7 and 12, B floors 7, 12 and 17) in the stair wells, with stringers, hole-side fences and two attic ladders. make.sh wrote a whole build.nbt with no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE lines (stairs line: 80 placed).
Each flight is walkable from its house's ground floor to every upper room in the box (A, B and C drawing rooms and bedrooms, and B's third floor). The attic is not reached: the shell leaves a solid floor cell at (4,17,23) and (26,17,23), and nothing backs the ladders at y=18..20.
Plan.md Notes and elements.md are updated (the stairs item is ticked, with the attic caveat noted).
polish: Attic unreachable: the shell's floor y=17 is solid at (4,17,23) and (26,17,23) (confirmed by probing build.nbt: spruce_planks), so the attic ladders have no hole to climb through. Fix needs an opening in the shell at those cells, or the ladder run extended down from y=13. Not fixed here because the cells are locked.

Attic ladders hang on nothing: (3,18..20,23) and (27,18..20,23) are empty, and the back wall above y=17 is empty too. `mcd check` reports 6 unsupported ladder cells. The roof or attic walls must supply a block behind each ladder cell.

Stringers of spruce_planks sit in the room air under each flight: (9,3,21),(9,4,22),(9,5,23) in A ground, (9,7..10) column cells in the upper floors, and the same pattern at x=21 for C and x=13 for B. The room designers must treat these as built, not as free floor.

Rail gap: the fence on the hole side runs along each riser except the top one, which leaves the top step open as the brief asks. The fences float above hole air and `mcd check` does not flag them, so the lamplighter should check the well for light, since it is never lit by this part.

End-to-end walk from the front door was not verified: the front door belongs to the fenestration part, which is not built yet. I checked each house from a ground-floor cell with temporary rooms files in /tmp/part2-test instead.

waste.what: Worked out the flight geometry by hand: the plan's 4-step stairFlight tops out at feet level 7 and the upper room is at 8, so I reasoned through riser heights, the exit direction and the stringers cell by cell.
waste.cost: about 15 minutes of reasoning, plus one helper run to confirm the risers
waste.tool: a stairFlight option for the exit cell (topY and exitDx) that also places stringers under risers over hole air, and a flight-level check that the top riser meets floor level plus 1 with headroom

waste.what: Verified walkability by writing temporary rooms.json files (entrance in each house's ground floor) because mcd walk from the real entrance reports every room UNREACHABLE until the front part is built.
waste.cost: 3 small json files and 3 walk runs
waste.tool: mcd walk --entrance <x,y,z> flag (or a --from option), so a part can test its own stairs before the front door exists

waste.what: Probed individual cells of build.nbt to confirm the attic hole and the missing wall behind the ladders, one node script at a time.
waste.cost: 1 probe script
waste.tool: mcd cell build.nbt x,y,z (print a cell's block and state) or mcd check listing each missing support as a coordinate

companions.task: Lay the mansard attic walls at y=18..20 behind the ladders at x=3/27 and z=24 (or the mansard's inner face), so each ladder cell has a block to hang from.
Cut the shell's floor hole at (4,17,23) and (26,17,23), since the cells are locked to the shell and the attic ladder needs the hole to climb through.
Light the stair wells, which are dark at the flight's underside, with a lantern hung under the upper floor's beam or on a wall-mounted fence arm.

summary:
roofs: parts/roofs.mjs builds the A and C townhouse mansards (dormers, keeps for the B face and the stacks), the B slate parapet roof (modern preset, plain eave, parapet 2), the B eave course at y=17, the quartz bracketed cornice at y=22 with brackets at y=21, and the canted-bay decks at y=12.
make.sh gives a whole build.nbt; the roofs line shows 805 placed, no REFUSED writes, no OFF-PALETTE blocks. `mcd check` reports no floating or unsupported blocks from the roofs; the front elevation shows the two mansards with dormers and B's parapet and cornice.
The portico top (entablature y=7, rail y=8) is not built here: elements.md puts it in the fenestration part (front.mjs). The chimney stacks are not built in this copy, so the roof-to-stack junction is unchecked.
polish: The portico top (entablature at y=7 and balcony rail at y=8, x13..17 z9..11) is not built: elements.md assigns the portico to the fenestration part (front.mjs), and building it here would collide with that part's writes.

The mansards use a custom slate mix (deepslate_tile 70, polished_blackstone_brick 25, cracked_deepslate_tiles 5) instead of the library's dark-slate palette, because dark-slate contains cobbled_deepslate and tuff bricks whose stairs and slabs are not in palette.json. plan.md's ROOFS table still says dark-slate: a plan.md Note should record this. I did not edit plan.md, since other workers may be writing to it.
The chimney stacks are not built in this copy (the chimneys part is a stub here), so the roof-to-stack junction is unverified. The roof keeps are in place at x10..12 and x18..20, z18..19, y18..28.
The canted-bay decks at y=12 are built, but the bay bodies and glazing belong to the shell and front parts, so the canted bay item in elements.md stays unticked.

The dormer x positions come from the townhouse preset (centred on each mansard's north face), not forced to x=7 and x=23 as plan.md says. The render shows them centred on each house; I did not measure them cell by cell.

waste.what: Found out which library roof mixes are palette-legal by reading roof-texture.mjs and trying a build: the dark-slate and slate palettes use cobbled_deepslate and tuff bricks, whose stairs and slabs are not in palette.json, so the first two builds were OFF-PALETTE. I then wrote a custom { mix, eave, ridge, verge } material by hand.
waste.cost: 3 build cycles, about 4 minutes, plus reading roof-texture.mjs
waste.tool: a `mcd roof --spec roof.json --dry-run` that checks each mix entry and its stairs/slab forms against palette.json and proposes legal substitutes, or a palette-aware preset option (e.g. material: 'dark-slate@palette').

waste.what: Found the B cornice row was taken by the modern preset's own stair cornice (smooth_stone_stairs at y=22), and that the A/C overhangs ran over the B face at z=11. I fixed both by hand: eave plain on B, and a keep box for the B face.
waste.cost: 2 rebuilds and a hand-written peek script that prints blocks on the z=11 row
waste.tool: a roof dry-run that lists which cells each preset writes outside its footprint and which of them collide with a named box (here, the B face), and a `mcd peek build.nbt --row z=11 --y 17..24` command.

waste.what: bracketCornice returns a count in `skipped`, not an array, which I only found by crashing the build.
waste.cost: 1 failed run
waste.tool: document the return shape of the vocab helpers (skipped: count or cell list) in vocab/h2.mjs.

companions.task: lay the mansard and B parapet deck with the palette's deepslate and blackstone courses, and set the dormer windows and the verge.
cut and set the B eave course, the quartz cornice and brackets, and the stone coping along the parapet.
confirm the stacks at x10..12 and x18..20 (z18..19) pass through the roofs at the cells kept for them, and that the cap clears the B parapet.
